title: Cross-tenant customer export via tenant_id parameter
desc: The customer export endpoint accepts an optional tenant_id query parameter and passes it to the data layer, which uses it instead of the caller's own tenant. Any signed-in user can download the full customer list (names, emails, plans) of any other clinic by changing one parameter.
repro:
GET /api/customers/export?tenant_id=t_bright
Authorization: Bearer <token for u_ben, Acme Dental agent>
evidence: HTTP 200, CSV contains Brightside Clinic customers (e.g. "Sam Okafor").
impact: Full cross-tenant disclosure of customer personal data. This is the most serious class of bug in a multi-tenant SaaS: one customer can read another customer's data, which is reportable under GDPR and usually ends contracts.
fix: Never accept a tenant identifier from the request. Derive the tenant from the authenticated session only, and enforce it in the shared data layer so no endpoint can override it. Add Postgres row-level security as a second barrier.
fixed: v0.2.0: the parameter is ignored; TenantScope always filters by the session tenant. Retest returned only Acme data.

title: Insecure direct object reference on GET /api/invoices/:id
desc: The invoice lookup queries by invoice id only, without a tenant filter. A user who knows or guesses another tenant's invoice id can read its amount, status and customer reference.
repro:
GET /api/invoices/inv_b1
Authorization: Bearer <token for u_ben, Acme Dental agent>
evidence: HTTP 200 with Brightside Clinic invoice inv_b1.
impact: Cross-tenant disclosure of billing data. Invoice ids are short and sequential-looking, so enumeration is practical.
fix: Scope every lookup by tenant (where tenant_id = $session_tenant and id = $id) and return the same 404 for "belongs to someone else" and "does not exist".
fixed: v0.2.0: lookup is tenant-scoped; retest returned 404.

title: MCP tool accepts tenant_id from the model (prompt-injection data access)
desc: The list_customers tool exposes a tenant_id argument. The AI model fills tool arguments, so any text the model reads (a support ticket, an email, a document) can instruct it to pass another tenant's id. The server trusts the argument.
repro:
tools/call list_customers {"tenant_id": "t_bright"}
(as u_ben, Acme Dental agent, over the MCP HTTP endpoint)
impact: Same data exposure as TD-01, but reachable through prompt injection: an attacker never needs credentials, only a way to get text in front of the model.
fix: MCP tools must not take tenant, user or role identifiers. Resolve the principal from the transport (verified token) and apply it server-side. Treat every tool argument as attacker-controlled.
fixed: v0.2.0: no tool accepts a tenant id; extra arguments are dropped. Retest returned only Acme data.

title: Stripe webhook accepted without signature verification
desc: The /webhooks/stripe endpoint parses and acts on any JSON body. It does not check the Stripe-Signature header, so anyone on the internet can send fake payment events.
evidence: HTTP 200; open invoice inv_a2 changed to "paid".
impact: Unauthenticated attackers can mark invoices as paid (getting service without paying) or trigger any other webhook-driven state change.
fix: Verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body with the endpoint secret, compare in constant time, and reject events outside a 5-minute timestamp window.
fixed: v0.2.0: signature and timestamp verified; retest got HTTP 400 and the invoice stayed open.

title: Webhook events not de-duplicated; refunds double-counted on retry
desc: Stripe delivers events at least once and retries on timeouts. The handler processes every delivery and adds the refunded amount each time instead of storing Stripe's running total.
repro: Deliver the same signed charge.refunded event (amount_refunded: 2000) three times.
impact: Financial records drift from Stripe; refunds and revenue reports are wrong. Happens on its own during normal Stripe retries, and on purpose when combined with TD-04.
fix: Record each event id in a processed-events table and skip duplicates. Write absolute values from the event (Stripe's totals), never increments.
fixed: v0.2.0: events de-duplicated by id; refund total is set, not added. Retest: refunded_cents = 2000.

title: Refund tool missing role check, amount cap and human confirmation
desc: The issue_refund tool refunds immediately in one call, for any amount, for any signed-in role. The model can trigger it on its own, including after a prompt injection.
repro:
tools/call issue_refund {"invoice_id":"inv_a1","amount_cents":12000,"reason":"..."}
(as u_ben, an agent, not an admin)
evidence: Full $120.00 refunded by an agent with no confirmation step.
impact: Direct money loss. Business impact is higher than the CVSS score suggests, because one manipulated conversation can issue refunds.
fix: Split money-moving actions into request and confirm steps, restrict to admins, cap the amount the AI may start, bind the confirmation to the same user and a short expiry, and mark the tool as destructive so MCP clients ask the human.
fixed: v0.2.0: request_refund + confirm_refund, admin only, $500 cap, same-admin, 10-minute expiry, single use. Retest: agent denied, nothing refunded.

title: Role and tenant taken from token claims; downgraded users keep old rights
desc: If a token carries tenant_id and role claims, they are trusted without checking the database. A user who is downgraded or removed keeps their old role until the token expires (8 hours).
repro: Use a valid token minted with role=admin for u_cara, whose current role is viewer, and call create_ticket.
evidence: Ticket created by a user who is a viewer in the database.
impact: Revocation doesn't take effect; a fired employee or downgraded user keeps access for hours.
fix: Put only the user id in the token and load tenant and role from the database on each request (or keep tokens very short-lived with a revocation list).
fixed: v0.2.0: claims ignored; role and tenant loaded per call. Retest: denied.

title: Database error details exposed to the MCP client
desc: Unexpected errors are returned to the client verbatim, including raw Postgres messages.
evidence: Response: date/time field value out of range: "2026-13-45"
impact: Reveals the database engine and query structure, which helps an attacker craft further attacks; also puts internal details into AI conversation logs.
fix: Return generic messages for unexpected errors, log the detail server-side with a correlation id, and validate inputs strictly before they reach the database.
fixed: v0.2.0: unexpected errors return "internal error". Retest confirmed.

title: CSV export allows spreadsheet formula injection
desc: Customer fields are written to CSV unchanged. A value starting with =, +, - or @ becomes a live formula when staff open the export in Excel or Google Sheets.
repro: Set a customer name to =HYPERLINK("http://evil.test","Click") and export as an admin.
evidence: Exported cell contains the live formula.
impact: Phishing links or data-exfiltration formulas run in staff spreadsheets.
fix: Prefix cells that start with formula characters with a single quote and quote-escape every cell.
fixed: v0.2.0: formula characters neutralised. Retest: exported as text.

title: No audit trail of actions taken through MCP tools
desc: Tool calls made by the AI, including refunds and data reads, are not recorded.
repro: Run the checks above and inspect audit_log.
evidence: 0 rows after 9 tool and API actions.
impact: No way to investigate what the AI did, who asked it, or whether data was accessed after an incident.
fix: Log every tool call with tenant, user, tool, arguments and outcome, including denied calls, and alert on spikes of denials.
fixed: v0.2.0: every call logged, allowed or denied.
